validity.researcher_notes: The Ukrtransgaz chronology (operator history page, web archive capture of 2016) says that in 1987 the Kremenchuk - Ananiv - Bohorodchany trunk gas pipeline, 532.6 km, 1020 mm, was put into service. It lists the line under 1986 as well. Ukrainian Wikipedia gives 532 km, 1020 mm and up to 8.7 bcm/y, and cites the same chronology. A 2017 KPMG report lists the line as Kemenchug-Ananijiv-Ananjiv-Bohorodchani. The line is real and is a transmission trunk.

validity.researcher_notes: Gazprom is recorded as 100% owner of a line that lies entirely in Ukraine (Kremenchuk to Bohorodchany). The operator history shows only Ukrainian state operators. No page found names the present legal owner. The start country is recorded as Russia, but Kremenchuk is in Poltava region, Ukraine. The end is recorded as Ananiev, which is a waypoint, not the end.

validity.recommendation: Probable overlap with P1481 (Ananiv-Chernivtsi-Bohorodchany). Do not merge or delete until a source splits the line.
validity.researcher_notes: The chronology lists one line, Kremenchuk - Ananiv - Bohorodchany, 532.6 km. Moldovatransgaz lists Ananiev - Chernovtsy - Bogorodchany (P1481) at 1020 mm and 9.1 bcm/y, with 184.8 km in Moldova. Both follow the same compressor chain. The lengths do not add up: 532.6 minus 333 leaves 199.6 km for Kremenchuk to Ananiv, while that leg is about 300 km in a straight line. No source states how the two relate.

The Ukrtransgaz chronology (operator history page, web archive capture of 2016) says that in 1987 the Kremenchuk - Ananiv - Bohorodchany trunk gas pipeline, 532.6 km, 1020 mm, was put into service. It lists the line under 1986 as well. The line starts at Kremenchuk in Poltava region and ends at Bohorodchany in Ivano-Frankivsk region, all in Ukraine. The sheet has the start country as Russia, which is wrong. It also has the end as Ananiev, which is a waypoint. The corrected values are Ukraine and Bohorodchany.

The chronology and Ukrainian Wikipedia say the line was built and describe it in the present tense. Neither is dated 2024 or later, so neither shows current use. A KPMG 2017 report lists the line by name but gives no status. Searched Ukrainian and English for newer operator or regulator mentions and found none.

Operator is blank. Since 2020 the Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine runs Ukraine's trunk network, but no page found names this line under it. The older operator was Ukrtransgaz. Searched Ukrainian web pages for the line name with the operator and its development plan, and found none. Not staged without a page that names the line.

No source supports Gazprom as owner. The line lies wholly in Ukraine, and the operator history shows Ukrainian state operators. Nothing found names the present legal owner, so no replacement is staged. See the attribution concern.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: No source dated 2024 or later names this line. It is a Soviet-era trunk that fed the Balkan route, and Russian transit through Ukraine ended on 1 January 2025. Its present use is not documented. Absence of news is not evidence for a change, so no change is proposed.
